title: Taiwan unveils new 5-year quantum tech program to speed adoption
source_used: Commercial Times (工商時報, on the China Times site), read in Chinese; Digitimes first paragraph only
key_facts: Digitimes (6 Oct 2026, first paragraph only): Taiwan's National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) has announced details of its next five-year quantum research programme as Taiwan prepares to wrap up its current NT$8 billion (US$252.14 million) National Quantum Team project by the end of 2026.

Commercial Times (5 Oct 2026, Chinese, translated): after the first-phase national quantum team met its goals, the NSTC has opened the call for second-phase proposals, a 'Quantum Leap Project research plan'.

It encourages teams to build, within five years, a real working quantum computing hardware system and a long-distance quantum communication protection network, joined with software engineering and hybrid computing platforms, to speed industry use.

Stated aim: use national-team resources to build a self-reliant, complete quantum ecosystem and play to Taiwan's strengths in chip manufacturing, IC design, silicon photonics and advanced packaging; named hardware parts include cryogenic Cryo-CMOS control chips, superconducting parametric amplifiers, high-efficiency single-photon detectors and quantum communication chips.

Phase one started in 2022 as a joint effort of the NSTC, Academia Sinica and the Ministry of Economic Affairs; the NSTC says it produced competitive superconducting qubit chips, silicon spin qubits and cryogenic readout and control modules, plus city-to-city quantum key distribution.

Quantum technology is one of the priority items in next year's science and technology budget; the earlier national strategy has a northern verification platform running and a southern HPQC computing centre due in 2029.
The report gives no budget figure for the second phase.
quote_evidence: The National Science and Technology Council (NSTC) has announced the details of its next five-year quantum research program as Taiwan prepares to wrap up its current NT$8 billion (US$252.14 million) National Quantum Team project by the end of 2026.
量子科技為明年度科技預算重點投入項目之一，繼第一期量子國家隊完成目標，國科會展開第二期計畫徵求，提出「量子躍昇專案研究計畫」，鼓勵五年內組建出真實可運算的實體量子運算硬體系統，與長距離量子通訊防護網絡，並結合軟體工程與混合式運算平台，加速推動產業應用落地。
量子國家隊第一期計畫於2022年整合啟動，由國科會、中研院及經濟部共同組成，今年3月國科會也發布高速量子運算國家戰略，主委吳誠文曾介紹，第一期已成功研發出具競爭力的超導量子位元晶片與矽基自旋量子位元，及低溫讀取與控制模組。
why_it_matters_hint: Taiwan's next five-year state quantum programme targets working hardware and long-distance quantum communication, building on its chip industry.
event_date: Call for second-phase proposals reported 5 Oct 2026 (Commercial Times print edition, online 4 Oct 20:10 UTC); the exact announcement date is not stated (Wearn says 'recently').
notes: The Digitimes page (the pool item) is readable only to its first paragraph (about 250 characters, subscription wall) and no other English outlet carries the story, so the details were read in the Chinese-language Commercial Times; EBC (news.ustv.com.tw) carries the same text and Wearn (news.wearn.com) shows only a teaser that agrees (5-year NT$8 billion plan ends 2026; next five-year plan recently announced). English names are our translation: 'Quantum Leap Project' is our rendering of 量子躍昇專案; Digitimes calls phase one the 'National Quantum Team'. No budget figure for phase two in anything read. Not carried in the previous 14 Full Reports.
